cards.title: Explicit evidence relations reduce avoidable abstention.

fields_tex.Prediction and endpoint: the revised scope rules and relation schema reduce unnecessary abstention on answerable unseen claims without exceeding a prespecified increase in incorrect definite judgments.
fields_tex.Comparison: frozen original versus revised single-pass systems, followed by a rules-by-schema factorial ablation.
fields_tex.Controls: identical evidence and model digest, held-out records and dates, independent scope/truth labels, blinded adjudication, clustered inference, and failures included in an overall endpoint.
fields_tex.Decision: support requires the abstention reduction and the false-certainty guardrail together. A coverage increase alone fails the claim. The existing twelve-case result selects a candidate; it does not estimate a transportable effect.
fields_tex.Readiness: protocol specification and independent labels required; no novel physics required.

cards.title: Blinded challenge helps through error diversity.
cards.status: partial computational diagnostic; no observed aggregate gain

fields_tex.Prediction and endpoint: hiding the verifier's verdict from the challenger lowers selective error at a prespecified common coverage.
fields_tex.Comparison: blind versus informed challenger within the same three-role architecture, plus a single-pass baseline matched on actual resource budget.
fields_tex.Controls: identical source families, randomized arm order, separate measurements of joint verifier/challenger mistakes, truncation, tokens, and latency.
fields_tex.Decision: no error reduction at matched coverage/cost, or a benefit explained entirely by refusing more cases, fails the proposed advantage. Equal total output allowance does not by itself equalize repeated input cost or truncation risk.
fields_tex.Readiness: engineering experiment; the saved pilot currently gives no three-role accuracy gain.

cards.title: Adaptive forgetting improves the recurrence--change tradeoff.

fields_tex.Prediction and endpoint: a causal mixture of forgetting rates improves equally weighted held-out scenario-average Brier loss relative to the best fixed rate selected on the same validation mixture, subject to worst-scenario and stationary-regime harm limits.
fields_tex.Comparison: selected fixed rate, adaptive mixture, uniform mixture, no memory, and TTL.
fields_tex.Controls: common paths, disjoint seeds, prequential scoring, identical shadow base/archive for weighting ablations, and separate replacement-policy factors.
fields_tex.Decision: lack of improvement over the strongest selected baseline or violation of the guardrail fails the bounded claim. Phase 2.9's short-dwell counterexample rules out unconditional benefit.
fields_tex.Readiness: the original Phase 2.10 bundle lacks a dependency and a complete test package. The isolated version 3 experiment supplies these locally and evaluates a specific frozen comparison; broader robustness remains open.

cards.title: Provenance awareness resists duplicated and stale evidence.

fields_tex.Prediction and endpoint: source-ancestry and time metadata reduce increases in false definite judgments under duplication or obsolete-report perturbations while preserving appropriate use of genuinely new evidence.
fields_tex.Comparison: metadata present versus ablated with paired, truth-preserving perturbations: duplicates, independent corroboration, superseded reports, unavailable current records, and authentic but irrelevant quotations.
fields_tex.Controls: equalized context/source budgets, blinded semantic labels, fixed underlying propositions, and record-level clustering.
fields_tex.Decision: unwarranted certainty rises materially under duplicate/stale evidence, or independent corroboration cannot be distinguished from copying. Numerical confidence scoring is a new endpoint if added; it cannot be inferred from the existing verdict labels.

cards.version_3_execution: Integrity/stress tests; no metadata-ablation factorial or semantic-benefit estimate.

cards.title: Fixed-count population bits are insensitive to pure dephasing.

fields_tex.Prediction: under Proposition~\ref{prop:bits}, bit-value distributions and their likelihood have zero dependence on the dephasing rate.
fields_tex.Comparison: retain path-basis bits versus recombined, phase-resolved interference data from the same stipulated dynamics.
fields_tex.Observable: likelihood derivative or estimated rate information, not a post hoc bit imbalance.
fields_tex.Controls: known preparation, readout basis, independence, fixed count, and timing exclusion; the interference model must retain nuisance contrast and phase.
fields_tex.Failure interpretation: parameter dependence in the exact stipulated bit model rejects the implementation or an assumption. A laboratory bias suggests preparation, readout, population transfer, or another mechanism; it is not distinctive support for rate-only physics.
fields_tex.Readiness: analytic and software test available now; it does not require a claimed field detection.

cards.title: Quadratic-portal decoherence has a constrained spatial shape.

fields_tex.Prediction: the massive thermal weak-coupling point-probe model gives zero rate at coincident paths, quadratic small-separation scaling, a finite saturation value, and the stated low-temperature activation.
fields_tex.Observable: $-\log(V/V_{\rm ref})/\tau$ over several separations, durations, and independently characterized bath states; a ratio at two nonzero rates removes the shared coupling.
fields_tex.Comparison: the full kernel versus conventional noise mechanisms and a generic fitted damping curve, with identical nuisance treatment.
fields_tex.Decision: a jointly incompatible shape rejects the frozen bath/portal/apparatus model after quantified systematics. Agreement does not uniquely identify a scalar. No signal cannot reject arbitrarily weak coupling or absent bath population.
fields_tex.Readiness: conditional numerical curve supplied here; finite trajectories, composite form factors, bath preparation, and power remain open.

cards.title: One portal parameter must fit both width and visibility.

fields_tex.Prediction: Eq.~\eqref{eq:cross} holds when the same scalar, normalization, mass, and portal account for Higgs decay and the prepared probe environment.
fields_tex.Observable: a joint likelihood for the width and visibility kernel with independently constrained bath occupation and nuclear inputs.
fields_tex.Comparison: a single shared coupling versus unrelated effective amplitudes, including ordinary decoherence.
fields_tex.Decision: no allowed shared parameter region rejects the specified common explanation, conditional on nuisance and model adequacy. A width upper limit by itself supplies no lower bound on visibility loss.
fields_tex.Controls: invisibility assumptions, thresholds, data overlap, total-width conventions, and absence of double counting.
fields_tex.Readiness: algebraic bridge available; no joint empirical fit or new exclusion is reported.

cards.title: Calibrated rate modulation obeys a composition constraint.

fields_tex.Observable: a source-factorial rate contrast with positive rates and fixed channel/readout.
fields_tex.Comparison: exponential, linear-response, saturating, and ordinary environmental models over a predeclared range.
fields_tex.Decision: a contrast incompatible with zero rejects additive exponential response under the calibrated source assumptions. Small-signal agreement is weak discrimination because many models share a linear Taylor term.
fields_tex.Controls: independent field/source calibration, baseline drift, nonlinear source transfer, nuisance rates, and held-out amplitude levels.
fields_tex.Readiness: source and apparatus objects remain open; cognitive or ethical labels are not calibrated physical sources.

cards.version_3_execution: No calibrated source-factorial experiment or physical data.

cards.title: Exact finite-radius kernels split the local mixed quartics.

fields_tex.Prediction: for the fixed supplied operator, profile, radius, and scalar convention, $C_0+C_1=2A_4$ while $C_1/C_0\simeq1.59179265$, not one.
fields_tex.Comparison: independent block-exponential and Cauchy-contour implementations, increased angular cutoffs, and the local approximation.
fields_tex.Proposed tolerances: absolute coefficient agreement $10^{-9}$ and sum-identity residual $10^{-10}$, to be frozen alongside precision and cutoff rules. These tolerances are new protocol choices, not observed errors.
fields_tex.Decision: persistent disagreement after controlled convergence rejects the stated calculation; recovery of unequal coefficients does not reject it.
fields_tex.Readiness: independent computational replication can proceed from the saved package. Physical masses require further normalization and vacuum matching.

cards.title: The protected photon direction survives the scalar response.

fields_tex.Prediction: neutral alignment and the stipulated charge imply $M^2N=0$, while the kinetic residue follows the quoted quadratic response.
fields_tex.Comparison: an independent full external-Clifford finite-momentum implementation versus the saved reduction.
fields_tex.Observable: a scale-normalized mass-null residual, the scalar--gauge Ward relation, and a remainder scaling as $O(h^4)$ after subtracting the quadratic term under uniform field rescaling.
fields_tex.Decision: a residual surviving precision/cutoff control or a remainder inconsistent with the $O(h^4)$ bound rejects the specified calculation. Roundoff near zero must be controlled.
fields_tex.Readiness: computational test; photon masslessness is common to other gauge theories and is not distinctive empirical confirmation of this construction.

cards.title: A complete benchmark must pass coupled consistency.

fields_tex.Gate, not an assumed positive prediction: in one frozen scheme solve joint radius/scalar stationarity and flatness, require positive physical kinetic eigenvalues and an acceptable normalized Hessian after removing gauge directions, then compute and cancel the appropriate higher-dimensional anomalies with stipulated fields/counterterms.
fields_tex.Comparison: exact treatment versus controlled truncations inside their own domains.
fields_tex.Decision: no admissible solution in a rigorously covered domain, a forbidden physical instability, or an uncancelled irreducible anomaly rejects that benchmark. An unsuccessful bounded numerical search is only a bounded search result.
fields_tex.Controls: fixed allowed parameters and counterterms; no unregistered rescue term.
fields_tex.Readiness: unresolved theoretical work. Success would establish conditional consistency, not observed unification.

cards.title: A fixed light spectrum predicts relative running slopes.

fields_tex.Prediction: in a predeclared threshold-free interval with the stipulated active matter, Eq.~\eqref{eq:running} fixes the relative inverse-coupling slope.
fields_tex.Observable: multi-scale scattering observables translated using a single matching scheme and covariance model.
fields_tex.Comparison: the frozen joint slope vector versus alternatives with different independently specified spectra; constant matching offsets may float.
fields_tex.Decision: incompatible slopes reject that spectrum/completion at the declared perturbative accuracy. Choosing thresholds from the same test data destroys the claimed out-of-sample prediction.
fields_tex.Controls: physical masses, hypercharge normalization, thresholds, higher-order errors, and correlated datasets.
fields_tex.Readiness: phenomenology and spectrum audit required, especially for the four chiral generations. No measured running fit is performed here.
